benchmark.title: CIS Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS 10.x/11.x Benchmark

checks.title: Ensure Telnet and HTTP are disabled on Management Interface Profiles
checks.command: show config running | match "(telnet yes|http yes)"
checks.rationale: Unencrypted HTTP and Telnet protocols expose administrator sessions and API keys to interception and credential harvesting.
checks.remediation: set network profiles interface-management-profile <profile-name> telnet no http no

checks.title: Ensure idle administrator timeout is set to 15 minutes or fewer
checks.rationale: Automated session termination mitigates the risk of unauthorized administrators or attackers utilizing abandoned workstations.

checks.title: Ensure permitted IP addresses are restricted for management interface access
checks.rationale: Restricting permitted IP ranges ensures management daemon endpoints are inaccessible from unauthorized subnets and rogue clients.

checks.title: Detect overly permissive security rules (from any to any service any allow)
checks.command: show running security-policy | match "from any to any .* service any .* action allow"
checks.rationale: Permitting all sources to all destinations without specific application profiles defeats Next-Generation Firewall inspection.
checks.remediation: Replace blanket any-any rules with zero-trust source zones, destination address objects, and strict App-ID specifications.

checks.title: Detect unrestricted inbound access to sensitive ports (SSH 22, RDP 3389, SMB 445)
checks.rationale: Exposing administrative or protocol-level sharing ports to untrusted public networks exposes the perimeter to credential brute force and exploits.
checks.remediation: Delete untrusted inbound rules for management services and require GlobalProtect VPN tunnel verification.

checks.title: Ensure default-deny interzone and intrazone drop rules log at session end
checks.rationale: By default, PAN-OS does not log dropped packets on the implicit interzone-default rule. Logging at session end is required for threat visibility.
checks.remediation: set rulebase default-security-rules rules interzone-default log-end yes

checks.title: Ensure security rules enforce application-default service port mappings
checks.rationale: Using application-default prevents evasion techniques where malware runs protocols over non-standard open ports.
checks.remediation: Edit security policy rules and set Service to application-default.

checks.title: Ensure remote Syslog server forwarding profile is configured
checks.rationale: Forwarding traffic, threat, and system logs to a centralized SIEM guarantees retention compliance and correlation across firewalls.
checks.remediation: set shared log-settings syslog <profile-name> server <server-name> server <syslog-ip>

checks.title: Ensure NTP time synchronization servers are configured
checks.rationale: Clock drift disrupts certificate expiration checks, App-ID cloud updates, and incident log sequencing.
checks.remediation: set deviceconfig system ntp-servers primary-ntp-server <primary-ip> secondary-ntp-server <secondary-ip>

checks.title: Ensure cleartext SNMPv1/v2c default community strings are removed
checks.rationale: SNMPv1/v2c sends community strings in cleartext and public/private defaults allow unauthorized state queries. SNMPv3 with authPriv is required.
